definitions.explanation: The time of day when the sun sets and darkness begins to fall.

examples.japanese: {日暮|ひぐ}れまでに{帰|かえ}ろう。
{日暮|ひぐ}れの{空|そら}が{美|うつく}しい。
examples.english: The sky at dusk is beautiful.

examples.japanese: {夏|なつ}は{日暮|ひぐ}れが{遅|おそ}いので、{長|なが}く{外|そと}で{遊|あそ}べる。
examples.english: Since sunset is late in summer, you can play outside for a long time.

notes:
Refers to the time when the sun sets and daylight fades. Emphasizes the transition from day to night, often implying a deadline — things that should be done before dark.

ETYMOLOGY:
Compound of {日|ひ} (sun/day) + {暮|く}れ (setting, ending). Literally "the day's end."

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {日暮|ひぐ}れまでに: by sunset/nightfall
- {日暮|ひぐ}れの{空|そら}: the sky at dusk
- {日暮|ひぐ}れが{早|はや}い/{遅|おそ}い: sunset is early/late (seasonal)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {夕暮|ゆうぐ}れ: evening, twilight (very close, slightly more poetic and literary)
- {日没|にちぼつ}: sunset (technical/formal, as in weather reports)
- {夕方|ゆうがた}: evening (more everyday, refers to the time period)
- {黄昏|たそがれ}: dusk, twilight (literary)
